items.text_excerpt: Chipotle is bringing back its Pollo Asado for a limited time with an all-new recipe featuring "freshly grilled adobo chicken seasoned with garlic, Mexican spices and hand-cut cilantro" and introducing Chili Lime Chips, available exclusively for Chipotle Rewards members beginning Aug. 31 before becoming available to all customers on Sept. 4.

Chipotle CEO Scott Boatwright doubled-down on a promise that customers can always get larger portions if they simply ask, but social media's more vocal sect isn't buying it. One user called Boatwright "clueless" and said the company is "getting eaten alive by their competitors." Another user claimed the dedicated fanbase that Chipotle used to enjoy is beginning to decline. "CEO is one of the most out of touch people I've seen," they wrote.

According to Downdetector, reports of issues began surging around 4:15 p.m. EDT on Sunday, with many frustrated customers taking to social media to complain that the outage had "ruined Father's Day." Customers attempting to place pickup or delivery orders reported a range of issues, including login failures, error messages, slow-loading pages, and checkout problems.

Chipotle's app and website were experiencing degraded performance on Father's Day, June 21, 2026, blocking customers from placing digital orders during one of the busiest restaurant days of the year. Outage monitoring service Entireweb logged 14 user error reports within a single hour. Affected customers reported login failures, payment processing errors, and "Something's not right, try again later" message.

Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc. beat allegations the fast-casual restaurant chain and executives defrauded investors by denying shrinking portion sizes as customer accusations went viral on social media. The investor leading the case didn't plausibly allege Chipotle reduced the size of its portions from 2021 to 2024, Judge Sherilyn Peace Garnett said.

Customer alleges their local Chipotle skimped on the chicken 'again.' Then they notice an employee's meal: '3x the size of mine'. Chipotle's portion consistency and the perception that employees get larger portions than customers remained an ongoing social-media flash point.

Chipotle wins lawsuit over portion sizes (article dated Sep 22, 2026 in the 180-day window). The case was dismissed by Judge Sherilyn Peace Garnett who said the plaintiff failed to adequately plead executive Laurie Schalow and former CEO Brian Niccol's repeated denials about portion size reductions were false or misleading.

Chipotle Mexican Grill announced its first-ever simultaneous launch of two limited-time menu items, bringing back Pollo Asado with an all-new recipe and introducing Chili Lime Chips, a new side inspired by a viral fan food hack. Pollo Asado returns to restaurants in the U.S. and Canada on August 31.

Chipotle Brings Back Pollo Asado with New Recipe and Introduces New Chili Lime Chips. Pollo Asado returns to all U.S. and Canada restaurants with a brand-new adobo chicken recipe; Chili Lime Chips debut exclusively for Rewards members on Aug. 31 before going wide on Sept. 4.

Chipotle (CMG) reported Q1 2026 revenue of $3.1B with comparable sales returning to positive territory at +0.5% and transactions growing 0.6%, marking its first quarter of positive growth in over a year. Digital sales reached 38.6% of food and beverage revenue; Chipotle's return to positive transaction growth on the back of its Recipe for Growth strategy involving high-protein menu offerings.

A company promotion announced on September 21 offers free quesadillas with a qualifying digital purchase on September 24 and September 25, as People reported. Stock closed at USD 33.42 on the NYSE on September 21, 2026, unchanged at 0.00 percent.

Vivian (Sarasota, FL): "Scandalous experience. Total was $6.10. Gave cashier a $20. Returned $13.00. I said where is the .90 cents. Then started shouting that I was bitching over a dollar. MY DOLLAR and SHE was the one bitching. Absolutely the WORST retail experience I have ever had."

Billy (Pittsburgh, PA): "Beware. Chipotle appears to be scamming people in online orders and not providing refunds. I used the app to try to resolve it and it was an AI chatbot confirmed the order but instead of refunding me it gave me a point rewards coupon for a free item instead of a refund."

Lisa Maria (Dallas, TX): "In my frequently visitations to the restaurant at 5290 Beltline Rd, Dallas, Tx 75254, Manager (and other managers) are always friendly and helpful in making my experience one to remember. The food is fresh, counters are clean, and the lobby is welcoming to dine in. I highly recommend this location."
Flight (Hershey, PA): "Food was dry. Doesn't take cash for some unfathomable reason like a normal restaurant. Cashier says this was posted. Yet I looked and nothing was there."

David (Henderson, NV): "I had a very disappointing experience at this Chipotle location on Sunset Road in Henderson. When I arrived, nearly all of the dining tables were dirty and hadn't been cleaned. The serving line was running low on several items, and they were out of tortillas, dressings, and even steak. Some of the employees did not appear to be very clean."

Terence (Aurora, CO): "Customer service is horrible. I remember when you could get a order from there for 10$. Now it's super over priced and the quality is not great. I can go to a food truck and get it cheaper and more satisfying. I don't recommend Chipotle to anyone."
Bonnie (Marina, CA): "Ordered a burrito for my son and found metal shavings in it. He almost swallowed it."

S (Tacoma, WA): "Picked up my order from Tacoma Pearl St location and they gave me someone else's order. The container was smashed as if they were not happy. I complained it was wrong. This is unacceptable and will not return to Chipotle. I want a full refund."

A (Lake Zurich, IL): "I am filing this complaint regarding a recent experience with Chipotle and the company's failure to provide a fair resolution. The portions were significantly smaller than expected, several ingredients were unavailable. Instead of addressing the issues I described, I was offered a BOGO promotion, which I do not consider an appropriate resolution."
Stel (Niles, OH): "Need reported to health board!!!! Rotten food, wilted and unwashed brown lettuce and left over crap!@!"

Anita (Winchester, VA): "BE AWARE: If you receive an offer from Chipotle on your Rewards list account stating 50% off an entrée, 815 points ... they will charge you the other half in money, so you will be using your points and your dollars to get it. It is misleading customers. It is false advertisement."

Noralinda (Alameda, CA): "On April 18 2026 I emailed Chipotle that I was complaining about my food and I found avocado skin in my guacamole. I asked for the same free steak burrito bowl but they denied my request."

Sandra (Houston, TX): "There was an advertisement poster stating 'Unlock free guac Scan to become a new rewards member & get free guac instantly.' They charged me for the guac. I reminded the employee of what the sign said. The manager said, 'i will call the police.' I encouraged all my family & friends to not dine there."

Helen (Phila, PA): "Got a coupon in my email for a buy one get one free to use on my app and it will not accept it and it expires in 3 days, I have contacted customer service 4 times and they tell me to send proof of the email so I did this twice and they never got back to me! Customer service is the absolute worst."

John (North Charleston, SC): "This is the 2nd time that I have been to this particular location where they have been out of KEY items. I specifically came in for the al pastor chicken, only to be told it would be another 15 minutes before it was ready. When I expressed my disappointment, the employee responded, 'We only have one grill person—you can come back and help if you want something.'"

C (Manvel, TX): "I was racially profiled and deeply offended by the manager! The manager's name is Esaul. I do plan on pursuing legal action towards him and the store. It is NOT ok for him to speak to people the way he does."

Crystal (Calhoun, GA): "I had yet ANOTHER bad experience at my local Chipotle in Calhoun, GA. ZERO customer service!! It's like they do that entire thing ON PURPOSE so they can tell you to screw off.... CHIPOTLE SUCKS!!!!"

A (Lake Zurich, IL): "A few weeks ago I received an email promotion from Chipotle. The picture in the email said 50% off an entree and 815 points. Since you can redeem 1625 points to get a free entree, so I interpreted the promotion as redeeming an entree using roughly only half of the normal points. Essentially I paid the full price, half with points and half with money."

E (Hacienda Heights, CA): "My review is not about the restaurant service but the use of their gift cards. I would advise customers to never purchase a gift card as I discovered they lose their value. But Chipotle takes it a step further by devaluing your gift card for each year you do not use it. I had a $15 gift card which only had a value of over $11 when I finally used it."

Sabrina P Kdo (Newark, Delaware): "Terrible service and even worse food! It was at the Chipotle at ***. My mom and I went to *** last night to order food for the family. We walked in and immediately thought they were closing due to there being no lettuce, cheese, sour cream, corn salsa. All of the meat and beans were dried, crusty, and stuck to the bottom of the pan... If we ever do go back to any Chipotle, it definitely will not be the one near us!"
Mario M Aok (Reno, Nevada): "As I was eating my dinner last night after picking up the chipotle I found a hair inside my food I had moved the hair to the top so its visible."

Brittany K Xux (Cleveland, Ohio): "Brown guac and inconsistent portions. At the Snow Road Parma location: -Brown/black almost guac, -Crunchy rice, -Inconsistent meat portions, -Inconsistent rice portions. Cons: Rude employees, Rotting avocados, Rotting lettuce."

Shane M Ntb (Chicago, Illinois): "Bogo is not helpful to me. I am single and never need two bowls. Please make the resolution so I can benefit from the original mistake. Preferred solution: Price reduction."

Shyler Ggz (Portland, Oregon): "Reward code says i've used it, when i haven't bought anything with it yet. I tried making an order a few minutes before, and then I closed the app for a second. Now the reward will not work, and is saying I already used it, when I know I didnt! I just wanted 50% off my entree, and now Ive been dealing with this issue for probably 20 minutes. The pepper chat bot they have for issues doesn't work either."

One user: "You ask and get 'a pinch more' then get charged for double," wrote one user, followed by a sobbing emoji. "Well yea, they don't say 'no.' They say 'I'll have to charge you for double meat,'" concluded another.

One person wrote on X, "Hey chipotle your app is down and I'm starving trying to order!" Another: "Chipotle what's up with the site man." Another: "Hey Chipotle. The app is down and stores don't know how to make the high protein burrito!!!"

Chipotle Mexican Grill, Inc. traded between USD 32.78 and USD 33.67 before ending at USD 33.42. The session range was USD 0.89, while the stock stayed within its 52-week range of USD 28.03 to USD 42.81. A company promotion announced on September 21 offers free quesadillas with a qualifying digital purchase on September 24 and September 25.

Chipotle (NYSE:CMG) just delivered its first quarter of positive transaction growth in over a year. With the stock down 34.46% over the past 12 months and trading near multi-year lows, the setup looks compelling. Chipotle's return to positive transaction growth on the back of its Recipe for Growth strategy involving high-protein menu offerings and high-efficiency equipment is reversing momentum from 2025's negative comparable sales.
Those who order online made sure that their interests were represented, as well. "How can you be a ceo and be this out of touch. What about the huge amount of people who order online?" someone asked.

Candy (Greeley, CO): "I'm a third party delivery driver and while waiting for my order I saw a sign on a stool 'don't seat down on this chair'. If this is how young people spell today, shame on all the teachers and professors that didn't teach them correctly or ignored the misspelled words."

John (North Charleston, SC): "When I expressed my disappointment, the employee responded, 'We only have one grill person—you can come back and help if you want something.' That comment was both surprising and unprofessional. At this point, I would prefer a refund rather than a 'free drink' on a future visit, as I don't plan on returning to this location—even though it's the closest to my home."

To celebrate the return of Pollo Asado, Chipotle is offering free delivery on Pollo Asado orders placed through the Chipotle app and website from Aug. 31 through Sept. 13. The Chili Lime Chips will be available exclusively for Chipotle Rewards members beginning Aug. 31 before they become available to all customers on Sept. 4. On Sunday, Sept. 6, customers who order two or more entrées after 3 p.m. local time on the Chipotle app or website can receive a free entrée using code "SUNDAYS."

The investor leading the case didn't plausibly allege Chipotle reduced the size of its portions from 2021 to 2024 or that the company was investigating whether its employees were skimping on servings. The case represented social-media backlash being formalized as a securities class action.

Customer alleges local Chipotle skimped on the chicken 'again.' Then they notice an employee's meal: '3x the size of mine'. The portion inconsistency narrative continued to draw user-generated content on social media in August 2026.

Rapper Cardi B appeared to accidentally leak the news of Chipotle's new Chili Lime Chips on social media before its official launch date. TMZ posted a screen recording of Cardi B's Instagram Live on Aug. 27 where she appeared to promote the new side item. Someone off camera tells her that she wasn't supposed to tell the public yet to which she replies, 'I wasn't supposed to tell y'all about the chips because the chips come out on Monday. Oops! My bad! I'm too excited!'

Update: As of 10:30 p.m. EDT, many of the reported issues appeared to have been resolved, though some users continued to report intermittent problems. Chipotle has not yet issued an official statement regarding the cause of the outage or when services were fully restored.

The combination — holiday foot traffic, promotion-driven app sessions, and Sunday dinner-rush hours typically running from 5:30 PM to 7:30 PM ET — created exactly the peak load scenario that Chipotle's digital platform has repeatedly failed to absorb in the past.
